neighbours.label: The modal or auxiliary in a second clause after 'While' or 'but', just before an expected ' also' ('While it can work ..., it can', 'but it can', 'but we're'); the same word in a lone clause stays low.
fire: While the tool can cut wood, it can also shape metal.
That may be true, but it can also be risky.
"We're fixing the roof, but we're also painting the barn."
While she can sing opera, she can also rap.
It might save time, but it could also cost more.
While this drug can ease pain, it may also cause sleep.
He can be kind, but he can also be cruel.
"They're cutting taxes, but they're also raising fees."
quiet: The tool can cut wood, so it can save time.
That is true, and it is risky.
She can sing opera in French.
It might save time because it could run faster.
This drug can ease pain in the back.
He can be kind to the dogs.

short: modal before an expected ' also' after a contrast
notes: Probes: 0.49-0.68 in that frame; lone clauses 0.01-0.05; a second sentence 0.11-0.17. Two near misses keep a second clause with no contrast. The card has many cases outside this frame (' You can', ' He has'), so it is narrower than the pole. The output direction promotes ' also', ' aussi', ' también'.
